title: Digital Learning Labs for Underserved Schools in Baden-Württemberg
description: Bosch's matched-giving initiative equips 50 state schools in socially disadvantaged areas of Baden-Württemberg with tablets, maker kits, and intensive teacher training programmes. Every euro donated through LBBW Legato is matched 1:1 by Bosch corporate giving, making donor impact immediate and tangible. The project aims to close the digital skills gap for 12,000 primary school pupils by 2027, with independent evaluation built into the programme design.
impactUnit: €200 equips one classroom with a full digital learning set for an entire school year

title: Schwarzwald Watershed Restoration Programme
description: A Bosch-funded landscape restoration programme working with the State Forestry Authority of Baden-Württemberg to replant drought-damaged sections of the Black Forest with climate-resilient native tree species. The programme also rehabilitates stream banks to improve water quality and flood retention. Bosch matches every donated euro, and donors receive geo-tagged updates on their trees throughout the growing season.
impactUnit: €50 plants and maintains one native tree for three years

title: AI-Powered Food Bank Logistics for Urban Germany
description: SAP's CSR giving fund supports the nationwide digital transformation of food bank operations, deploying SAP-developed inventory and donor management tools to cut food waste and improve distribution efficiency. The programme directly serves over 200,000 food-insecure people across Berlin, Hamburg, and Munich. Donors co-fund alongside SAP's corporate giving budget, with real-time impact dashboards accessible through LBBW Legato.
impactUnit: €30 covers one month of emergency food supplies for one person

title: Code & Future: Digital Skills for Refugee Youth in Germany
description: SAP's matched-giving programme funds intensive digital skills workshops for 16–25 year old refugees, delivered in partnership with Germany's federal integration agencies. Participants gain certified competencies in programming, data literacy, and workplace IT tools, dramatically improving their labour market prospects. The programme has already supported over 800 young people and aims to scale to 3,000 by 2026.
impactUnit: €150 funds one week of digital skills training for one refugee young person

title: Emergency Fleet Deployment for Disaster Relief in Southeast Europe
description: Mercedes-Benz's corporate giving programme donates and maintains a fleet of adapted vans and minibuses for disaster relief organisations operating in flood and earthquake zones across Southeast Europe. The matched-giving initiative allows donors to co-fund vehicle maintenance, driver training, and emergency supply logistics through LBBW Legato. The fleet has supported responses in 14 disaster events since 2022.
impactUnit: €500 covers one month of maintenance and fuel for one relief vehicle

title: Safe Futures: Road Safety Education for Children in Low-Income Communities
description: Mercedes-Benz's global road safety programme brings interactive traffic safety education to primary schools in underserved communities across Germany, Romania, and Morocco. The initiative trains local teachers, provides physical education kits, and reaches approximately 60,000 children per year. Corporate co-funding matches donor contributions, with programme expansion driven by the total amount raised through Legato.
impactUnit: €25 funds a full road safety education kit for one child

title: Solar Schools: Clean Energy for Rural Education in Sub-Saharan Africa
description: Porsche's 'Road to Zero' philanthropic giving initiative funds rooftop solar installations at rural schools in Tanzania and Ghana, providing reliable electricity for the first time to learning environments that previously relied on diesel generators or had none at all. Each installation powers classrooms, libraries, and water pumps for up to 25 years. Donors co-fund alongside Porsche's corporate commitment, and matched donations are tracked in real time on LBBW Legato.
impactUnit: €1,000 provides one school with one year of solar-powered electricity

title: Second Chance: Employability Programme for Long-Term Unemployed Adults
description: Porsche's 'Chance' employability fund supports intensive 12-week vocational retraining programmes for long-term unemployed adults in Stuttgart and its surrounding region, run in partnership with social enterprise carriers. Graduates gain certifications in automotive and technical trades, with 68% securing employment within three months. Donors contributing through Legato benefit from Porsche's 2:1 match on all donations above €500.
impactUnit: €300 funds one week of vocational training for one long-term unemployed adult

title: MakerSpace Networks for STEM Education in Rural Schools
description: TRUMPF's corporate giving initiative equips rural secondary schools across Germany with professional fabrication tools — laser cutters, 3D printers, and CNC machines — donated from their product range and supported by certified teacher training. Each MakerSpace serves multiple schools in a region, enabling hands-on STEM learning that was previously only available in city centres. Donors fund the consumables, networking events, and curriculum content that make each MakerSpace sustainable.
impactUnit: €500 funds one month of materials and consumables for a rural MakerSpace serving five schools

title: Precision Reforestation with LiDAR-Guided Planting in German Forests
description: TRUMPF's precision technology expertise meets environmental philanthropy in this initiative, deploying drone survey and LiDAR analysis to identify optimal reforestation sites in damaged German woodlands before planting begins. The result is a 40% higher tree survival rate compared to conventional methods, and carbon sequestration figures are independently verified and reported to donors quarterly.
impactUnit: €80 plants ten trees in precision-identified optimal locations with a 95% survival guarantee

title: Apprenticeship Access Programme for Young People from Disadvantaged Backgrounds
description: Würth's corporate giving fund pays for bridging training, mentoring, and initial toolkits for young people from low-income families entering skilled trade apprenticeships across Germany. The programme removes the financial barriers that cause many promising candidates to drop out before completing training. In its first three cohorts, 94% of supported apprentices completed their qualification.
impactUnit: €400 funds a full starter toolkit and first-year mentoring for one apprentice

title: Palliative Care Units for Rural Hospitals in Baden-Württemberg
description: Würth's health-focused giving programme co-funds the establishment and staffing of palliative care units in small district hospitals across rural Baden-Württemberg, where such services have historically been unavailable. The fund targets facilities serving communities of under 30,000 people where the nearest existing palliative ward is more than 40 km away. Donor contributions are matched 1:1 by the Würth Group's charitable trust.
impactUnit: €200 funds one day of specialist palliative nursing care for one patient

title: Adaptive Mobility Solutions for Disabled People in the Global South
description: ZF Friedrichshafen's giving initiative leverages the company's mobility engineering expertise to donate and adapt wheelchairs, hand-cycles, and assistive transport vehicles for distribution in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia through NGO partners. The programme targets communities where 90% of mobility aid needs go unmet. Every donation through Legato funds both the hardware and the local technician training required to maintain it.
impactUnit: €350 provides a fully assembled and fitted wheelchair to one person in need

title: Minds Matter: Mental Health Support in Secondary Schools
description: ZF's employee-matched giving fund supports embedded school counsellor positions and peer-support training programmes in secondary schools across the Lake Constance region. The initiative addresses the growing gap between adolescent mental health needs and available professional support, targeting a counsellor-to-student ratio of 1:250. Since launch, participating schools have reported a 34% reduction in serious safeguarding incidents.
impactUnit: €100 funds one hour of certified school counselling for a student in crisis

title: Microinsurance for Smallholder Farmers in East Africa
description: Allianz's philanthropy fund co-finances agricultural microinsurance for subsistence farmers in Kenya and Tanzania, protecting families against crop losses caused by drought, flood, and pest outbreaks. The product is designed specifically for farmers earning under €500 per year, with premiums subsidised through charitable donations. A successful harvest gives farmers confidence to invest in improved seeds and tools, breaking the poverty cycle.
impactUnit: €40 covers one season of crop insurance for one smallholder farming family

title: Climate Resilience Fund for Flood-Affected Communities in Germany
description: Following the 2021 Ahr valley floods, Allianz established a long-term resilience fund to help communities in flood-prone areas of Germany upgrade housing and infrastructure with flood-resistant materials and early warning systems. The fund targets households that cannot access conventional insurance, specifically in the middle Rhineland and Eifel regions. Donor contributions are matched by Allianz's foundation at 50 cents per euro.
impactUnit: €1,000 funds flood-resistant retrofitting for one room of a vulnerable household

title: Age-Friendly Workshop Programme for Active Seniors
description: Festo's corporate giving initiative funds practical skills workshops — electronics, digital tools, and creative making — designed specifically for adults over 65 who want to remain engaged with technology and avoid social isolation. Delivered by Festo-certified trainers at community centres across Baden-Württemberg, the programme improves both cognitive health and social connection for participants who complete the six-week course.
impactUnit: €60 funds a full 6-week workshop course for one senior participant

title: Automated Urban Greening Systems for Heat-Stressed Cities
description: Festo's biomimetics-inspired CSR initiative deploys automated vertical garden systems on public buildings in Stuttgart and Mannheim, reducing urban heat island temperatures by up to 4°C in surrounding streets. The living walls use Festo's precision irrigation control systems donated at cost, while donor funds pay for plant material and annual biological maintenance. Each installation serves as a research site for biodiversity and urban cooling monitoring.
impactUnit: €500 installs and maintains 10 square metres of certified urban green wall for one year

title: Low-Carbon Building Materials for Social Housing in Germany
description: Heidelberg Materials' foundation fund subsidises the use of low-carbon concrete and recycled aggregate in social housing construction projects, targeting a 40% reduction in embodied carbon per building. Donor contributions co-fund the premium cost difference between standard and green materials, enabling housing associations with tight budgets to make sustainable choices without financial penalty. The fund currently supports 12 housing projects across the Rhine-Neckar metropolitan region.
impactUnit: €2,000 covers the green premium cost of low-carbon concrete for one social housing unit

title: Earthquake-Resistant School Construction in Türkiye
description: Following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake, Heidelberg Materials partnered with UNDP and local NGOs to fund the construction of earthquake-resistant primary schools in the affected region using advanced structural techniques and certified materials. The giving initiative rebuilds community anchors while creating local construction jobs and upskilling local builders in seismic-safe methods. Sixteen schools are planned, with five already operational and serving 2,800 children.
impactUnit: €5,000 funds the earthquake-resistant structural elements for one classroom

title: Welcome Kits and Integration Support for Refugee Families in Germany
description: dm's corporate giving programme assembles and distributes welcome kits containing essential personal care products, hygiene supplies, and German language learning tools to newly arrived refugee families in Germany, reaching over 50,000 people annually. Volunteer networks in dm stores facilitate distribution and provide warm first contact for arriving families. Donor contributions through Legato are matched by dm at 100%, doubling the impact of every gift.
impactUnit: €35 provides a fully stocked welcome kit for one refugee family member for the first month

title: Menstrual Health Dignity Programme for Women Experiencing Homelessness
description: dm's social responsibility fund supplies quality menstrual hygiene products to women's shelters and street outreach services across Germany's 50 largest cities, addressing a frequently overlooked dimension of poverty. The programme trains shelter staff in dignified product provision and educates on menstrual health, ensuring recipients feel respected rather than stigmatised. dm covers logistics costs so 100% of donated funds go directly to product provision.
impactUnit: €15 provides a full year's supply of menstrual hygiene products for one woman experiencing homelessness

title: Open-Source Early Warning Platform for Climate Disasters in Vulnerable Regions
description: Vector Informatik's giving initiative funds the development and deployment of an open-source disaster early warning platform used by civil protection authorities in Southeast Europe and East Africa. Built on Vector's embedded software expertise, the platform aggregates meteorological, seismic, and hydrological sensor data to generate alerts 48–72 hours before extreme events. All code is made freely available to governmental agencies globally.
impactUnit: €100 covers one month of server infrastructure supporting early warning for 100,000 people

title: Digital Financial Inclusion for Rural Communities in West Africa
description: Vector's corporate giving fund co-finances the deployment of offline-capable digital financial tools for rural communities in Ghana and Senegal, where mobile network coverage is unreliable and formal banking is inaccessible. The platform, built in partnership with local fintech NGOs, enables savings groups, microloan management, and supplier payments without needing continuous internet access. Over 15,000 farmers and small traders have enrolled since the 2024 pilot.
impactUnit: €50 onboards and supports one rural community member on the digital finance platform for one year

title: Community Solar for Social Housing Estates in Baden-Württemberg
description: EnBW's community energy giving programme installs rooftop solar arrays on social housing blocks and community buildings, transferring ownership to residents' associations after a 5-year period and eliminating energy poverty for hundreds of households. Donor funding bridges the gap between grant funding and installation cost, making each project financially viable. EnBW provides all technical planning and grid connection at no charge as its corporate contribution.
impactUnit: €1,500 installs enough solar capacity to cover the annual electricity needs of one social housing apartment

title: Solar-Powered Clean Water Access for Rural Kenya
description: EnBW's international giving fund co-finances solar-powered borehole drilling and water purification units for rural communities in the Rift Valley region of Kenya, where women and children walk an average of 4 km each day to collect unsafe water. Each installation serves approximately 500 people and eliminates waterborne disease exposure for a generation. EnBW provides technical expertise for the solar pump systems, while donor funds pay for borehole drilling and community water board training.
impactUnit: €500 provides one person with safe, clean piped water for their entire lifetime

title: Cold Chain Technology for Vaccine Distribution in the Sahel
description: Liebherr's precision refrigeration giving initiative donates solar-powered vaccine cold-chain units to district health centres in Niger, Mali, and Chad, where electricity supply is unreliable and vaccine spoilage rates average 42%. The programme is designed in partnership with WHO and UNICEF, and Liebherr's field technicians provide installation and two-year maintenance support. Donor contributions fund the shipment and community health worker training component.
impactUnit: €200 protects one child's complete vaccination schedule through solar cold-chain storage

title: Alpine Peatland Restoration for Carbon Sequestration
description: Liebherr's nature giving fund partners with Bavarian and Austrian conservation authorities to restore degraded peatlands in the Alpine foothills, which are among the most carbon-dense ecosystems in Europe. Restoration work involves rewetting, vegetation transplanting, and long-term hydrological monitoring. Independent third-party carbon measurement ensures full transparency for donors on the climate impact of their contribution.
impactUnit: €100 permanently restores 10 square metres of functioning peatland ecosystem

title: Mobile Medical Clinics for Conflict-Affected Populations in the Middle East
description: Daimler Truck's humanitarian vehicle giving programme donates and maintains converted truck-based mobile medical clinics for deployment in conflict zones in Syria, Yemen, and Gaza through Médecins Sans Frontières. Each unit provides emergency surgery, trauma care, and maternal health services in areas where fixed medical infrastructure has been destroyed. Donor funds pay for medical supplies and the local medical staff training embedded in each unit.
impactUnit: €500 funds one day of full operations for a mobile medical clinic serving up to 80 patients

title: Youth Sport for Cohesion: Football Academies for Refugee Integration
description: Daimler Truck's social cohesion giving fund supports community football academies in German cities with large refugee populations, using sport as a structured pathway to language learning, friendship networks, and vocational mentoring. Academy coaches receive specialist intercultural training, and the programme links participants to employment and apprenticeship opportunities with partner companies. The programme currently operates in Stuttgart, Ulm, and Friedrichshafen.
impactUnit: €200 covers six months of football academy participation, coaching, and mentoring for one refugee young person

title: Energy Poverty Relief Programme for Families in Baden-Württemberg
description: Caritas Baden-Württemberg's flagship winter relief fund provides emergency energy bill support, insulation upgrades, and energy advice to families who cannot afford adequate heating. Last year, the programme prevented 3,200 households from having their heating disconnected during winter months. Donations through LBBW Legato are pooled and allocated by trained Caritas social workers to verified cases within 48 hours of referral.
impactUnit: €150 covers one month of heating costs for one vulnerable family during winter

title: Emergency Shelter and Transitional Housing for People Fleeing Domestic Violence
description: This Caritas programme maintains a network of emergency refuge places and transitional housing units across Baden-Württemberg for women and children fleeing domestic violence. Each placement includes psychological support, legal advice, and children's counselling. Demand consistently exceeds capacity by 35%, and donor funding directly enables the opening of new safe places across the region.
impactUnit: €100 funds one night of emergency shelter, counselling, and support for one person fleeing violence

title: School Feeding and Nutrition Programme in the Sahel
description: Deutsche Welthungerhilfe operates school feeding programmes in Niger and Burkina Faso that provide the only guaranteed daily meal for 85,000 children enrolled in partner schools. The programme increases school attendance by 40%, especially for girls, while improving nutritional outcomes and reducing stunting. Local food purchasing agreements stimulate regional agricultural markets and create sustainable supply chains.
impactUnit: €50 feeds one child a nutritious school meal every day for one full school term

title: Resilient Seeds and Climate-Smart Agriculture in Ethiopia
description: Welthungerhilfe's agricultural resilience programme distributes drought-tolerant seed varieties and provides farmer training in conservation agriculture techniques across drought-prone regions of Ethiopia. The initiative targets households that have experienced at least two harvest failures in the past five years, prioritising women-led farming families. Outcomes from the 2023 pilot show a 55% increase in yields in participating communities compared to a control group.
impactUnit: €80 provides one farming family with a full season of resilient seeds and expert agronomic support

title: Climate Justice: Amplifying Voices from the Global South
description: Welthungerhilfe's policy and advocacy programme amplifies the voices of communities most affected by climate change in international forums, UN negotiations, and German public discourse. The programme trains local leaders from Bangladesh, Sudan, and the Philippines to present evidence-based testimonies, funds translation and participation costs, and produces multilingual media content. Every contribution through Legato directly supports a climate-affected community spokesperson.
impactUnit: €200 funds one community advocate's preparation, travel, and testimony at an international climate forum

title: Citizen Science Biodiversity Monitoring Across German Nature Reserves
description: NABU Naturschutzbund coordinates a nationwide citizen science programme that trains volunteers to monitor bird, insect, and plant populations across 300 protected nature reserves in Germany. Data collected feeds directly into federal biodiversity reports and conservation planning decisions. Donor funding supports volunteer training materials, digital reporting tools, and the expert biologists who validate the results.
impactUnit: €40 trains and equips one citizen scientist for a full year of biodiversity monitoring

title: Urban Wildflower Corridors: Pollinators in German Cities
description: NABU's urban biodiversity initiative works with city authorities and housing associations to transform underused urban green spaces into wildflower meadows and insect-friendly habitats, creating pollinator corridors connecting fragmented nature reserves. The programme has already transformed over 80 hectares across Hamburg, Berlin, and Cologne. Donor contributions fund seed mixes, maintenance training for municipal gardeners, and long-term population monitoring.
impactUnit: €60 plants and maintains 100 square metres of certified urban wildflower meadow for one season

title: River Rewilding and Fish Migration Restoration on German Rivers
description: NABU leads a landscape-scale river restoration programme removing obsolete weirs and fish barriers from the Rhine, Elbe, and Main river systems, reopening hundreds of kilometres of migration routes for salmon, trout, and eel. Each weir removal also improves flood dynamics and water quality for downstream communities. Engineering costs are covered jointly by federal grants and this donor fund, with LBBW acting as the disbursement partner.
impactUnit: €1,000 funds the engineering survey and preparation work to remove one river barrier, reopening kilometres of fish habitat

title: Inclusive Playgrounds and Accessible Public Spaces for Disabled Children
description: Aktion Mensch's flagship inclusion fund co-finances the redesign of public playgrounds and community centres to be fully accessible to children with physical and learning disabilities. Each project is co-designed with disabled children and their families, and certified by independent accessibility auditors. To date, 340 playgrounds across Germany have been transformed, benefiting an estimated 28,000 children.
impactUnit: €300 funds one piece of certified inclusive play equipment accessible to children of all abilities

title: Arts and Dementia: Creative Therapy Programmes in Care Homes
description: Aktion Mensch's quality-of-life giving programme funds professional artists, musicians, and storytellers to lead regular creative therapy sessions in dementia care homes across Germany. Clinical evidence consistently shows improvements in cognitive function, mood, and social connection among participants. Donor funding covers artist fees, materials, and staff training in supportive facilitation.
impactUnit: €150 funds one month of weekly creative therapy sessions for one dementia care home resident

title: First Aid Training for 100,000 Schoolchildren Across Germany
description: Deutsches Rotes Kreuz's school programme trains secondary school students in certified first aid, defibrillator use, and emergency response through a dedicated curriculum delivered by DRK youth trainers. Early bystander intervention triples survival rates in cardiac emergencies; Germany currently has one of the lowest rates of bystander CPR in Europe. Donor funding covers the cost of training materials, manikins, and trainer certification for under-resourced schools.
impactUnit: €25 trains one schoolchild in certified first aid and defibrillator use

title: Psychosocial Support for Disaster Survivors in Germany
description: DRK's mental health response programme embeds trained psychosocial support teams in disaster-affected communities for up to 12 months following major flood and storm events, addressing the severe psychological trauma that often outlasts physical reconstruction. The 2021 Ahr valley flood aftermath demonstrated that psychosocial needs persist for years; this programme ensures survivors are not left without support. Teams provide individual counselling, group processing sessions, and community resilience workshops.
impactUnit: €80 funds one hour of certified psychosocial support for one disaster survivor

title: SOS Villages for Orphaned and Abandoned Children in East Africa
description: SOS-Kinderdorf operates family-style residential communities in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda for children who have lost parental care, providing a nurturing home environment, quality schooling, and vocational training. Each SOS Village houses 150–200 children in family units of 8–10 with a long-term primary caregiver. Donor contributions through Legato directly fund the ongoing care and education costs of children in these communities.
impactUnit: €80 covers one month of full care, nutrition, and schooling for one child in an SOS Village

title: Child Protection and Anti-Trafficking Programmes in Southeast Asia
description: SOS-Kinderdorf's child protection programme operates awareness campaigns, community guardianship networks, and legal advocacy to prevent child trafficking and exploitation in Thailand, Vietnam, and Cambodia. Trained community volunteers identify at-risk children and trigger protective interventions before harm occurs. The programme has prevented an estimated 4,200 trafficking incidents since its 2019 launch.
impactUnit: €60 funds one month of trained community child protection monitoring in a high-risk village

title: Youth Empowerment and Leadership Academy for Care Leavers
description: SOS-Kinderdorf's post-care support programme prepares young adults leaving care homes for independent living through a 12-month leadership and skills academy, covering financial literacy, mental health, professional skills, and civic engagement. Alumni report dramatically improved self-efficacy and income stability. The programme operates in Germany, Austria, and Romania and has supported over 1,100 care leavers since 2020.
impactUnit: €500 funds one care leaver's complete 12-month empowerment and life-skills programme

title: Mobile Health Clinics for Homeless Populations in German Cities
description: Ärzte der Welt operates mobile medical units in Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, and Frankfurt providing free primary care, mental health consultations, and specialist referrals to people experiencing homelessness who are excluded from the statutory healthcare system. Each unit sees 80–120 patients per day. Donations fund the clinical supplies, pharmacy costs, and volunteer physician coordination that keep the units operational year-round.
impactUnit: €40 funds a full medical consultation, diagnosis, and treatment for one person experiencing homelessness

title: Maternal and Newborn Health in Conflict-Affected Zones of the DRC
description: Ärzte der Welt's obstetric emergency programme operates birthing clinics and trains traditional birth attendants in the conflict-affected provinces of North Kivu and Ituri in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where maternal mortality rates are among the highest in the world. A trained birth attendant prevents an average of two maternal deaths and six neonatal deaths per year. Donor funding covers medical supplies, training costs, and emergency evacuation kits.
impactUnit: €100 trains one traditional birth attendant, preventing multiple maternal and neonatal deaths annually

title: Legal Aid and Healthcare Access for Undocumented Migrants in Europe
description: Ärzte der Welt's access-to-rights programme provides confidential medical care and legal counselling to undocumented migrants and asylum seekers in Germany, France, and Spain who fear accessing public services. The multidisciplinary teams combine doctors, nurses, social workers, and lawyers in a single consultation environment, addressing the interconnected health and legal barriers faced by this population. Over 35,000 people were seen in 2024.
impactUnit: €60 covers one complete consultation — medical, social, and legal — for one undocumented migrant

title: Critical Habitat Protection for Large Carnivores in the Carpathians
description: WWF Deutschland co-funds wildlife rangers, habitat connectivity surveys, and coexistence programmes for wolves, bears, and lynx in the Carpathian mountain arc spanning Romania, Slovakia, and Poland. Human-wildlife conflict is the primary driver of illegal killing; the programme directly compensates shepherds for livestock losses and funds protective infrastructure. As flagship species, these predators signal ecosystem health for hundreds of dependent species.
impactUnit: €80 funds one day of wildlife ranger patrol protecting large carnivore habitat

title: Tiger Conservation and Anti-Poaching in the Sundarbans Mangroves
description: WWF's Sundarbans programme employs and trains local community members as anti-poaching rangers and wildlife monitors in the world's largest mangrove ecosystem, shared between Bangladesh and India. The initiative combines ranger-led enforcement with alternative livelihood programmes that reduce fishing communities' economic dependence on forest exploitation. Camera trap data show a 28% increase in tiger sightings since 2021.
impactUnit: €120 funds one month of full ranger salary, equipment, and patrol operations protecting tiger habitat

title: Marine Protected Area Enforcement in the Mediterranean
description: WWF Deutschland co-funds patrol vessels, monitoring technology, and legal advocacy to enforce existing marine protected area regulations in the Western Mediterranean, where illegal bottom trawling continues to devastate seabed ecosystems. The programme works with Italian, Spanish, and Greek coast guards and provides evidence packages to prosecuting authorities. Healthy marine ecosystems support the livelihoods of 30 million coastal people in the region.
impactUnit: €500 funds one day of joint patrol and monitoring operations covering 200 km² of protected marine habitat

title: Digital Media Literacy Programme for Primary Schools in Underserved Areas
description: Stiftung Bildung's nationwide programme trains primary school teachers in 300 schools in socially deprived areas to integrate digital and media literacy into everyday lessons, equipping children with critical online skills from the age of six. Teacher training workshops are certified by state ministries of education, and all curriculum materials are freely available for download. Independent evaluations show significant improvements in information literacy scores among participating pupils.
impactUnit: €200 trains one primary school teacher in certified digital media literacy pedagogy, benefiting 25 pupils per year

title: Language Integration Classes for Newly Arrived Refugee Children
description: Stiftung Bildung funds intensive German language support classes for recently arrived refugee children in the critical first 18 months after arrival, a period proven decisive for long-term educational integration. Trained specialist teachers work within mainstream school settings to provide daily immersive language support without separating children from their peers. The programme currently supports 4,500 children across 12 German states.
impactUnit: €120 covers one month of daily specialist language integration support for one refugee child

title: Legal Action Against Illegal Air Pollution in German Industrial Zones
description: Deutsche Umwelthilfe's environmental litigation programme brings legal cases against municipalities and industrial operators exceeding nitrogen dioxide and particulate matter limits in residential areas, forcing compliance with EU clean air standards. Legal victories to date have led to the introduction of low-emission zones covering 5 million residents. Donor funding covers court costs, expert scientific witnesses, and the monitoring equipment needed to build legally defensible cases.
impactUnit: €100 funds one hour of specialist environmental lawyer time bringing a clean air legal case

title: Consumer Information Campaign: Reducing Single-Use Plastic in Food Retail
description: Deutsche Umwelthilfe's consumer empowerment programme runs a mass-media and in-store campaign educating German consumers on alternatives to single-use plastic in food retail, supported by printed guides, digital content, and partnerships with 80 supermarket chains. The 2023 pilot in Bavaria reduced single-use plastic bag usage by 34% in participating stores. Donor funding scales the campaign nationally and funds legal monitoring of retailer compliance with the EU Single-Use Plastics Directive.
impactUnit: €50 reaches 500 consumers with evidence-based plastic reduction messaging and practical alternatives

title: Debt Counselling and Insolvency Prevention for Vulnerable Households
description: Caritas Baden-Württemberg's debt counselling service provides free, professional insolvency prevention advice to over-indebted households before crisis point is reached. Trained counsellors negotiate with creditors, restructure payment plans, and provide legal guidance that prevents eviction and family breakdown. Early intervention saves households an average of €8,500 in additional costs compared to formal insolvency proceedings.
impactUnit: €120 funds a complete debt counselling and restructuring process for one vulnerable household

title: Blood Donation Awareness and Mobile Collection Drives
description: Deutsches Rotes Kreuz's blood security initiative operates mobile donation buses and runs targeted awareness campaigns in underserved communities, universities, and workplaces where donation rates are below national averages. Germany currently faces periodic blood supply shortfalls; each mobile drive collects an average of 120 units per day. Donor contributions fund bus operation, donor experience improvements, and the digital registration infrastructure that reduces barriers to first-time donation.
impactUnit: €35 covers all costs of recruiting, testing, and processing one unit of donated blood that saves a patient's life

title: Trauma-Informed Care Training for Residential Youth Workers
description: SOS-Kinderdorf's professional development programme provides certified trauma-informed care training to residential youth workers across Germany, Austria, and Central Eastern Europe, transforming how they support children who have experienced violence, neglect, or loss. Professionally trained caregivers produce significantly better long-term outcomes for children in care; the programme targets 100% coverage for all SOS care workers by 2028. Donor funding pays for trainer salaries and the adaptation of curricula to local languages and legal contexts.
impactUnit: €400 provides one residential youth worker with full certified trauma-informed care qualification

title: Kelp Forest Restoration and Blue Carbon along the German Coastline
description: WWF Deutschland co-funds scientific expeditions and underwater restoration trials to re-establish kelp forests along the German North Sea and Baltic coastlines, where warming water temperatures and eutrophication have caused 80% losses since 1960. Restored kelp forests sequester carbon, support juvenile fish populations, and protect coastlines from erosion. Each hectare of kelp restored provides ecosystem services valued at €60,000 per year.
impactUnit: €500 funds the marine equipment and diver time needed to restore 100 square metres of kelp forest

title: Early Childhood Education Access for Children from Disadvantaged Families
description: Stiftung Bildung's early years programme funds nursery and kindergarten places for children from families receiving social welfare, addressing the critical window between birth and age six when educational experiences have lifelong impact. The programme subsidises the parental fee contribution that prevents access and provides trained family support workers who help parents create stimulating home learning environments. Investment at this stage produces a social return of €7 for every €1 spent, according to independent economists.
impactUnit: €200 funds one month of quality early childhood education for one child from a family unable to afford fees
